subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Conventional vs Electron Flow
description: A fast breakdown of Conventional vs Electron Flow for builders.

hook.text: Engineers draw current flowing one way. Electrons actually move the opposite way.

buildup.text: Benjamin Franklin guessed current flows from positive to negative. He was wrong.

discovery.text: Electrons carry negative charge and move from negative to positive terminal.

twist.text: By the time we knew, all equations were built on Franklin's convention.

climax.text: So engineers kept conventional flow. The math works either way.

punchline.text: The arrows point the wrong way — and nobody cares.

quiz.question: Why do circuit diagrams use conventional current flow?
options: Electrons actually do flow from positive to negative
All equations were built on that convention before the truth was known
Conventional flow is more accurate for AC circuits
